packs.title: Between River and Square
packs.promise: Find London in the shapes, gestures and small pauses between big sights.

q.s: Collect three small performances in the National Theatre’s exterior.
st: Stand aside on Queen’s Walk with a ground-level view of the National Theatre’s concrete terraces. No stairs or building entry are needed.
Find a horizontal ledge, a vertical face, and a shadow that joins them. Treat these as three pieces of a stage set.
Describe which shape seems closest and which seems farthest away; then pick one detail you would give the spotlight.
Save your three finds and your spotlight choice.

q.s: Write a tiny scene from a tree, a path and the sky.
st: Enter an open path at Jubilee Gardens from Queen’s Walk or Belvedere Road. Choose a comfortable spot away from the children’s playground.
Choose three ingredients: a tree detail, a curve in a path, and something the light is doing. Nothing needs to be picked up.
Write three short lines: one for what is still, one for what is moving, and one for where your attention goes next. Use your three ingredients in any order.
Read the lines silently and save them, with an optional photograph of the landscape.

q.s: Make one bridge crossing into a before-and-after story.
st: From the south approach to Waterloo Bridge, choose an open footway using signed crossings and the street-level approach. Do not take riverside stairs if they do not suit you.
Before crossing, choose one riverbank shape to remember: a roofline, bridge arch, or broad stretch of water.
Cross at a comfortable pace, keeping to the same footway. Stop only where there is room, and look for how the remembered shape changes.
At the far end, write “before” and “after” observations. A short out-and-back on one approach or two stationary views also completes the mission.

packs.title: Greenwich in View
packs.promise: Explore Maritime Greenwich through ship lines, small courtyard details and changing views.

q.s: Make a tiny composition from the space between buildings.
st: Choose an open public position in or beside Grand Square with a view of both domes. Follow current grounds signs.
Make three marks or phrases: one dome, the open space, the other dome. Then add one line that leads through the composition.
Compare the pair for one visible similarity and one difference. Keep those details in your drawing or note.

q.s: Separate a navigation object’s visible features from its story.
st: Choose an open free permanent gallery and one object connected to navigation or sea travel. Use its label to confirm the connection; paid exhibitions are unnecessary.
Write two features you can actually see, such as a scale, handle, curve, case or surface.
Add one question or tentative guess about its use. Then read the label and record one supported fact, keeping observation, guess and fact distinct.

q.s: Pause with shapes that remain when flowers change.
st: Choose an open path edge or available seat in the Flower Garden, leaving room for others.
For about a minute, notice one shape that holds still and one texture that changes with light or breeze. Trees, lawn edges and paths work without flowers.
Write the two observations and one word for the pace you want to keep. Leave all plants and materials where they are.
